requiredFindings.title: Member file-size ceilings are not a bound on the shared ledger charges
requiredFindings.finding: The new workspace term identifies its D15 observation bound only with item 19/X2's 4 MiB index and 64 KiB config ceilings. Those cap input lengths, not the ledger's cumulative requested bytes, objects or edges. The existing bounded reader charges every buffer growth before reading; a 4 MiB input can incur 12,578,817 buffer bytes, and git_tracking.rs additionally charges twice the index length for decoding, plus opens, status/custody and other work. The proposed row/cap rule therefore does not yet specify a sound complete-invocation cost bound.
requiredFindings.requiredCorrection: Require each workspace row to add a reviewed D15 ledger-cost upper bound in all three dimensions to its discovery cost before applying the 2x/power-of-two rule. Derive it from the member count and actual read-growth, decode, open/custody, retained-record and other charged operations, under an explicit retry envelope. Treat X2 input ceilings as inputs to that derivation, not as the charge itself. Pin the relevant cost closure or keep the full-ledger margin outstanding until the member producer/model is reviewed. Identify current option (a)/(b) figures as walker-only unless the completed bound is included.
